Use case: precise-object-edit.
Paint the first input image, the 1024 x 1024 orthographic white model guide, using the second input image solely as the design, colour and material reference for Lord Mraal's phase cleaver. Produce ONE 1024 x 1024 RGBA PNG with a truly transparent background.
ABSOLUTE GEOMETRY LOCK: the first input is the edit canvas. Preserve its alpha silhouette pixel for pixel, all empty margins, exact position, exact size, camera angle, part boundaries, holes and every edge. Change only RGB surface colour inside its existing opaque silhouette. Do not enlarge, recenter, rotate, redraw or add geometry. Keep all transparent pixels transparent. The large empty space is intentional for texture projection.
Material authority: second image. Match worn warm ivory/white ceramic bone-like plates and rib bands with fine restrained scratches; near-black violet resin/chitin with subtle purple mottling, fine etched seams; muted brushed antique gold only on thin existing trim; orange to pale warm yellow-white light within the existing blade edge and small recessed channels. Do not add blue, extra parts, text or letters. Continue these same materials plausibly on hidden surfaces.
LIGHTING: flat diffuse albedo texture source, shadowless even illumination from the viewer. Paint material base colours with only faint sheen. No cast shadow, no ambient occlusion darkening, no directional shading, no strong specular highlights, no reflection, no rim light, no floor, no background. Bright orange channels are solid bright light colours confined inside the geometry with no glow halo or light cast onto other parts. Fine surface marks only, no inscriptions.

FRONT VIEW: obey guide_front.png exactly. This is an extremely foreshortened end-on view, a SMALL horizontal silhouette only from x=331 to 692 and y=469 to 554 on the 1024-square canvas. Preserve the pointed tapered blade to the left and thicker irregular housing at the right; the long handle is occluded by this camera. Paint the visible end-on thickness only. Do not reveal a full axe or a side-on weapon. Preserve the almost empty canvas exactly.
